liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **phil** (3 reviews): Fragment holds Truckin', a Nobody's Fault jam, a Phil solo, and a Phil and Billy section into a groovy jam; Phil's section of the fragment is intense, best heard on headphones [4][10][13]
- **Truckin’** (1 other source): Uploader's list runs Truckin' into Nobody's Fault But Mine, then Eyes Of The World, then Sugar Magnolia [1]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Jerry uses a wah-wah around the 18-minute mark just before the jam returns from space [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **nobody’s dang fault doodle jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **phil**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [16]
- **groovy jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **uncle j’s jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-02-24.142031.aud.owen.berger.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 10 songs; 52 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd73-02-24.pset1-sbd.sly.16051.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 4 songs; 37 min; rated 4.71/5 by 17 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard of the Playin' In The Band set is rated excellent in sound quality [5]
- **gd73-02-24.sbd.elliot.11929.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 2 songs; 9 min; rated 4.68/5 by 19 [3]. Said about its sound: Phil's bass has a striking stereo image, as if some strings are panned left and others right; Wall of Sound wired each bass string to different speaker rows; better recordings capture that spread; Reviewer describes the soundboard fragment as a very high-quality recording [8][9][13]

## Around the show

- Iowa City fans have long hoped more of this soundboard material would surface [4]
- Reviewer calls this Playin' In The Band their favorite among the versions they have downloaded [6]
- Reviewer ranks this Playin' alongside University of Illinois and Eugene versions as their two favorites [7]
- Reviewer had never heard Phil play like this with the Dead and thinks similar examples are rare [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-02-24.142031.aud.owen.berger.flac1644**: taped by Mark Owen; transferred by Rob Berger; source: partial source: aud cassette master; taped by Mark Owen; sears & robuck deck, floor, 100’ from stage; nakamichi dragon > benchmark adc1 @ 24/96> adobe audition… [1]. Also: Audience-source recording, identified with Owen and Berger in the file name, circulating as FLAC [1]
- **gd73-02-24.pset1-sbd.sly.16051.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd73-02-24.sbd.elliot.11929.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by www.gratefulseconds.com: [Dead Sell-Out Iowa City, February 24, 1973](http://www.gratefulseconds.com/2018/08/dead-sell-out-iowa-city-february-24-1973.html) [17]
- Fan art by www.gratefulseconds.com: [Dead Sell-Out Iowa City, February 24, 1973](http://www.gratefulseconds.com/2018/08/dead-sell-out-iowa-city-february-24-1973.html) [18]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Poster University of Iowa 02.24.1973](https://www.dead.net/fanphotos/poster-university-iowa-02-24-1973) [19]
